verdict.rationale: Jitsu's self-hosting docs say it is "100% open-source", its llms.txt calls it an open-source platform, a public GitHub repo (jitsucom/jitsu) is cited, and a community user reports running "the open source version". So the source is readable and claimed to be open. However, no evidence names the license or confirms its terms, so the "under an open license" part is only implied. missing for 10: the specific license name and terms (e.g. a LICENSE file or license statement), independent confirmation that the entire product source, not just parts, is under that license.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: Jitsu is 100% open-source and can be deployed to any on-premise infrastructure.
Jitsu is an open-source data integration platform and a self-hostable alternative to Segment.
We've started using the open source version for one of the tools we are building
